fixes.explanation: That's what Mark says. In holding to the tradition of the elders, the Pharisees and all the Jews do not eat until they wash their hands ceremonially (Mark 7:3). The Pharisees are the strict religious leaders, and the writer says it's all the Jews, so this was a whole-community tradition. That's a lot of people washing before a meal.

Yes! They ask, "Why do Your disciples not walk according to the tradition of the elders?" (Mark 7:5). They add that the disciples eat with defiled hands. They saw unwashed hands and marched straight to Jesus with it. I think they were ready for a quick answer, but a whole lot more was coming.

The Sabbath does come up in other places, like when Pharisees question Jesus about His disciples picking grain (Mark 2:23-24). But not here. In this scene they ask why the disciples do not walk according to the tradition of the elders, and they point to eating with defiled hands (Mark 7:5). This complaint is all about hands and tradition.

Fasting is a real question people brought to Jesus in another place (Mark 2:18), but it's not on the table here. The Pharisees and scribes ask why His disciples do not walk according to the tradition of the elders, and they say the disciples eat with defiled hands (Mark 7:5). This complaint is about washing before a meal, not skipping one.

That's right. In the words Jesus quotes, "These people honor Me with their lips…" (Mark 7:6). It's the very next part that stings, because the quote goes on to say "…but their hearts are far from Me." (Mark 7:6). Honoring God with the lips while the heart is far from Him is exactly what Jesus is naming.

Not quite. The quote says they teach as doctrine "…the precepts of men." (Mark 7:7). That's the answer the verse gives, and the prophets' words aren't what it names. The trouble Jesus points to is rules that came from men.

The Sabbath shows up in other Pharisee arguments, like in Mark 2:24, so it's a fair guess. But in this verse Jesus says, "You have disregarded the commandment of God to keep the tradition of men." (Mark 7:8). The Sabbath isn't in this verse at all. The word that fits is commandment.

Good thinking, because Jesus does talk about what comes out of a man. He says the things that come out of a man are what defile him (Mark 7:15). But this question asks what can't defile, and Jesus says that's anything that enters a man from the outside. So this answer isn't the one Jesus names here.

That's right! Jesus says, "but the things that come out of a man, these are what defile him." (Mark 7:15). He's talking to the crowd He called to Him. The whole handwashing argument was about what goes in, and Jesus flips it to what comes out. Imagine scrubbing your hands for years and then hearing that.
